value: The purpose of adopting the young boy was to assist on the farm.
unit: Obed Abernethy resided at Grey Shutters in Brierley alongside his sister, Thirza. Struggling with advancing age, heart trouble, and difficulty securing hired labor, Obed persuaded Thirza to adopt a young boy from an orphanage in Nova Scotia to assist on the farm. Traveling to Alder River station to collect the child, he discovered an eleven-year-old orphan girl named Nell Harcourt instead of a boy due to a mix-up. Fearing to break the news immediately to the eager girl, he brought her back to Grey Shutters. Though Thirza initially insisted on returning Nell, Obed took a liking to her loquacious nature and quietly advocated for keeping her. Throughout Nell's upbringing, Obed consistently doted on her, buying her treats and supporting her desires, such as persuading Thirza to let her go to a local concert and purchasing a stylish puffed-sleeve dress for her. When the Abbey Bank unexpectedly failed, wiping out all of their savings, the sudden shock triggered a fatal heart attack, and Obed passed away in the porch doorway of his home.

label: History
value: Miss Agnes Thorne earned the affection of her pupils.
unit: Miss Agnes Thorne was hired as Brierley's first female schoolteacher in the autumn following Mr. Pidgeon's departure. She quickly earned the affection and dedication of her pupils through her gentle demeanor, refined manners, and innovative teaching methods, which included biweekly recitation Fridays, outdoor nature field days, and daily physical culture exercises. Recognizing the potential in her advanced students, she formed a dedicated after-school Entrance preparation class for those seeking admission to Regent's. Though she was offered a position at her home district's school at the end of her first year, she declined it to see her Brierley students through to their Entrance examinations. She continued guiding her scholars through their final academic year, holding rigorous drills, administering preparatory exams, and offering warm encouragement until her departure at the end of the term.
